page: Microsoft Azure D16_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores utilizing symmetric multiprocessing with two threads per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI for vector computations, alongside hardware AES cryptography acceleration.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per virtual core. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registers 82.97 GB/sec for sequential reads and 45.16 GB/sec for sequential writes, while small cached 16 KB read operations achieve 830.75 GB/sec. The D16_v4 does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring workloads to rely completely on network-attached block storage for persistence and operating system volumes. It also does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the D16_v4 squarely in the average tier across general compute and memory tests. It delivers a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,938.0 and a single-core score of 1,269.0, supplemented by a PassMark CPU score of 15,671.52. High-throughput tasks show steady efficiency, reaching 13.89 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 12.04 GB/sec for static web serving. For lightweight machine learning tasks, 135M parameter models achieve prompt processing speeds of 618.22 tokens/sec, but processing degrades to 22.86 tokens/sec when handling 7B parameter models, reflecting lower tier performance under heavier matrix loads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D16_v4 balances processing throughput with balanced memory capacity for workloads that do not demand transient local NVMe speed or GPU acceleration. The absence of local disk drives lowers hardware overhead for deployments utilizing decoupled remote storage architectures. This configuration fits enterprise web applications, intermediate relational database servers, build automation systems, caching nodes, and multi-threaded ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D16_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory balance. The host architecture does not include dedicated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance demonstrates middle-tier multi-core compute capability, registering a PassMark CPU score of 15,671.52 and supporting 13.89 million Redis SET operations per second. While small language model inference remains viable, larger model processing exhibits lower throughput due to CPU execution limits. The instance provides stable, balanced compute density for web application tiers, relational databases, continuous integration workers, and containerized microservices.
